sanskrit: rājyaṃ vai paramo dharma iti dharmavido viduḥ mahāntam etaṃ bhāraṃ ca manye tad brūhi pārthiva
english: The knowers of dharma declare that kingship is the highest dharma; yet I deem it a mighty burden. Speak to me of it, O king.

sanskrit: rājadharmān viśeṣeṇa kathayasva pitāmaha sarvasya jīvalokasya rājadharmāḥ parāyaṇam
english: Tell me in particular of the duties of kings, O grandsire; for the whole world of the living, the duties of kings are the final refuge.

sanskrit: trivargo 'tra samāsakto rājadharmeṣu kaurava mokṣadharmaś ca vispaṣṭaḥ sakalo 'tra samāhitaḥ
english: In the duties of kings, O Kaurava, the three aims of life are bound together, and the dharma of liberation too is plainly and wholly comprised therein.

sanskrit: yathā hi raśmayo 'śvasya dviradasyāṅkuśo yathā narendradharmo lokasya tathā pragrahaṇaṃ smṛtam
english: As the reins are to the horse and the goad to the elephant, so is the dharma of a king remembered to be the rein that guides the world.

sanskrit: atra vai saṃpramūḍhe tu dharme rājarṣisevite lokasya saṃsthā na bhavet sarvaṃ ca vyākulaṃ bhavet
english: If this dharma, honored by royal sages, fell into confusion, the world would lose its stability and all would be thrown into disorder.

sanskrit: udayan hi yathā sūryo nāśayaty āsuraṃ tamaḥ rājadharmās tathālokyām ākṣipanty aśubhāṃ gatim
english: As the rising sun destroys the demonic darkness, so do the duties of kings cast off the inauspicious course that leads from the bright worlds.

sanskrit: tad agre rājadharmāṇām arthatattvaṃ pitāmaha prabrūhi bharataśreṣṭha tvaṃ hi buddhimatāṃ varaḥ
english: Therefore, first of all, declare the very essence of the duties of kings, O grandsire, best of the Bharatas; for you are the foremost among the wise.

sanskrit: āgamaś ca paras tvattaḥ sarveṣāṃ naḥ paraṃtapa bhavantaṃ hi paraṃ buddhau vāsudevo 'bhimanyate
english: From you comes the highest tradition for us all, O scorcher of foes; for Vāsudeva himself accounts you supreme in wisdom.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca namo dharmāya mahate namaḥ kṛṣṇāya vedhase brāhmaṇebhyo namaskṛtya dharmān vakṣyāmi śāśvatān
english: Bhīṣma said: Homage to the great Dharma, homage to Kṛṣṇa the creator; having bowed to the brāhmaṇas, I shall declare the eternal duties.

sanskrit: śṛṇu kārtsnyena mattas tvaṃ rājadharmān yudhiṣṭhira nirucyamānān niyato yac cānyad abhivāñchasi
english: Hear from me in their entirety, O Yudhiṣṭhira, the duties of kings as I expound them, attentive and composed, and whatever else you desire to know.

sanskrit: ādāv eva kuruśreṣṭha rājñā rañjanakāmyayā devatānāṃ dvijānāṃ ca vartitavyaṃ yathāvidhi
english: At the very outset, O best of the Kurus, a king who desires to give joy to his people must conduct himself toward the gods and the twice-born according to ordinance.

sanskrit: daivatāny arcayitvā hi brāhmaṇāṃś ca kurūdvaha ānṛṇyaṃ yāti dharmasya lokena ca sa mānyate
english: By worshipping the deities and the brāhmaṇas, O upholder of the Kurus, a king becomes free of his debt to dharma and is honored by the world.

sanskrit: utthāne ca sadā putra prayatethā yudhiṣṭhira na hy utthānam ṛte daivaṃ rājñām arthaprasiddhaye
english: And in exertion, my son, always strive, O Yudhiṣṭhira; for without exertion, fate alone does not bring about the success of kings' aims.

sanskrit: sādhāraṇaṃ dvayaṃ hy etad daivam utthānam eva ca pauruṣaṃ hi paraṃ manye daivaṃ niścityam ucyate
english: These two together work in common—fate and exertion alike; yet I hold human effort to be supreme, while fate is said to be already determined.

sanskrit: vipanne ca samārambhe saṃtāpaṃ mā sma vai kṛthāḥ ghaṭate vinayas tāta rājñām eṣa nayaḥ paraḥ
english: And when an undertaking has failed, do not give way to grief; discipline labors on, my son—this is the highest policy of kings.

sanskrit: na hi satyād ṛte kiṃ cid rājñāṃ vai siddhikāraṇam satye hi rājā nirataḥ pretya ceha ca nandati
english: For apart from truth there is no cause of success for kings; a king devoted to truth rejoices both here and hereafter.

sanskrit: ṛṣīṇām api rājendra satyam eva paraṃ dhanam tathā rājñaḥ paraṃ satyān nānyad viśvāsakāraṇam
english: Even for the seers, O king of kings, truth is the highest wealth; and likewise for a king there is no greater ground of trust than truth.

sanskrit: guṇavāñ śīlavān dānto mṛdur dharmyo jitendriyaḥ sudarśaḥ sthūlalakṣyaś ca na bhraśyeta sadā śriyaḥ
english: Endowed with virtues, of good character, self-restrained, gentle, righteous, master of his senses, fair to look upon and large of aim—such a one never falls from prosperity.

sanskrit: ārjavaṃ sarvakāryeṣu śrayethāḥ kurunandana punar nayavicāreṇa trayīsaṃvaraṇena ca
english: In all your dealings hold to uprightness, O delight of the Kurus, tempered yet by the discernment of policy and by the safeguard of the three Vedas.

sanskrit: mṛdur hi rājā satataṃ laṅghyo bhavati sarvaśaḥ tīkṣṇāc codvijate lokas tasmād ubhayam ācara
english: A king who is always gentle becomes despised by all on every side; yet from one who is harsh the people recoil. Therefore practice both.

sanskrit: adaṇḍyāś caiva te nityaṃ viprāḥ syur dadatāṃ vara bhūtam etat paraṃ loke brāhmaṇā nāma bhārata
english: The brāhmaṇas must ever be exempt from punishment, O best of givers; for they are the highest order of beings in the world, those called brāhmaṇas, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: manunā cāpi rājendra gītau ślokau mahātmanā dharmeṣu sveṣu kauravya hṛdi tau kartum arhasi
english: Two verses were sung of old by the great-souled Manu, O king of kings; you ought to keep them in your heart amid your own duties, O Kauravya.

sanskrit: adbhyo 'gnir brahmataḥ kṣatram aśmano loham utthitam teṣāṃ sarvatragaṃ tejaḥ svāsu yoniṣu śāmyati
english: Fire arose from the waters, the kṣatriya from the brāhmaṇa, iron from stone; their all-pervading energy is quenched within their own sources of birth.

sanskrit: ayo hanti yadāśmānam agniś cāpo 'bhipadyate brahma ca kṣatriyo dveṣṭi tadā sīdanti te trayaḥ
english: When iron strikes the stone, when fire meets the waters, and when the kṣatriya turns in hatred against the brāhmaṇa—then those three come to ruin.

sanskrit: etaj jñātvā mahārāja namasyā eva te dvijāḥ bhaumaṃ brahma dvijaśreṣṭhā dhārayanti śamānvitāḥ
english: Knowing this, O great king, the twice-born are ever worthy of your homage; the best of the twice-born, possessed of tranquillity, uphold the earthly Brahman.

sanskrit: evaṃ caiva naravyāghra lokatantravighātakāḥ nigrāhyā eva satataṃ bāhubhyāṃ ye syur īdṛśāḥ
english: And even so, O tiger among men, those who would wreck the order of the world—such men must ever be held in check by force of arms.

sanskrit: ślokau cośanasā gītau purā tāta maharṣiṇā tau nibodha mahāprājña tvam ekāgramanā nṛpa
english: Two verses were sung long ago by Uśanas, the great seer, my son; mark them well, O most wise king, with single-minded attention.

sanskrit: udyamya śastram āyāntam api vedāntagaṃ raṇe nigṛhṇīyāt svadharmeṇa dharmāpekṣī nareśvaraḥ
english: Even one who has reached the end of the Vedas, if he comes weapon-raised against him in battle, a king mindful of dharma should strike down in keeping with his own duty.

sanskrit: vinaśyamānaṃ dharmaṃ hi yo rakṣati sa dharmavit na tena bhrūṇahā sa syān manyus taṃ manum ṛcchati
english: For he who guards dharma when it is being destroyed is a knower of dharma; by that deed he does not become a slayer of the unborn—the wrath of the offender falls upon himself.

sanskrit: evaṃ caiva naraśreṣṭha rakṣyā eva dvijātayaḥ svaparāddhān api hi tān viṣayānte samutsṛjet
english: And even so, O best of men, the twice-born must be protected; though they have offended, the king should but banish them to the edge of his realm.

sanskrit: abhiśastam api hy eṣāṃ kṛpāyīta viśāṃ pate brahmaghne gurutalpe ca bhrūṇahatye tathaiva ca
english: Even toward one of them accused of crime he should show compassion, O lord of peoples—whether in the slaying of a brāhmaṇa, the defiling of a teacher's bed, or the killing of the unborn.

sanskrit: rājadviṣṭe ca viprasya viṣayānte visarjanam vidhīyate na śārīraṃ bhayam eṣāṃ kadā cana
english: And for a brāhmaṇa hated by the king, banishment to the edge of the realm is ordained; never at any time should bodily punishment be visited upon them.

sanskrit: dayitāś ca narās te syur nityaṃ puruṣasattama na kośaḥ paramo hy anyo rājñāṃ puruṣasaṃcayāt
english: And these men should ever be held dear, O best of men; for kings have no greater treasury than a gathering of able men.

sanskrit: durgeṣu ca mahārāja ṣaṭsu ye śāstraniścitāḥ sarveṣu teṣu manyante naradurgaṃ sudustaram
english: Among the six kinds of fortresses determined by the treatises, O great king, in all of them the fortress of men is held the hardest to overcome.

sanskrit: tasmān nityaṃ dayā kāryā cāturvarṇye vipaścitā dharmātmā satyavāk caiva rājā rañjayati prajāḥ
english: Therefore the wise king must ever show compassion toward the four orders; a king righteous of soul and truthful in speech gives joy to his subjects.

sanskrit: na ca kṣāntena te bhāvyaṃ nityaṃ puruṣasattama adharmyo hi mṛdū rājā kṣamāvān iva kuñjaraḥ
english: Yet you must not be forever forbearing, O best of men; for an over-gentle, ever-forgiving king is unrighteous, like an elephant that suffers all.

sanskrit: bārhaspatye ca śāstre vai ślokā viniyatāḥ purā asminn arthe mahārāja tan me nigadataḥ śṛṇu
english: In the treatise of Bṛhaspati certain verses were laid down of old upon this very matter, O great king; hear them as I recite them to you.

sanskrit: kṣamamāṇaṃ nṛpaṃ nityaṃ nīcaḥ paribhavej janaḥ hastiyantā gajasyeva śira evārurukṣati
english: A king who is always forbearing the low-born will hold in contempt; like the driver of an elephant, the people will seek to mount upon his very head.

sanskrit: tasmān naiva mṛdur nityaṃ tīkṣṇo vāpi bhaven nṛpaḥ vasante 'rka iva śrīmān na śīto na ca gharmadaḥ
english: Therefore let a king be neither always gentle nor always harsh, but glorious like the sun in spring—neither cold nor scorching with heat.

sanskrit: pratyakṣeṇānumānena tathaupamyopadeśataḥ parīkṣyās te mahārāja sve pare caiva sarvadā
english: By direct observation, by inference, by analogy, and by instruction, O great king, your own people and your foes alike must always be examined.

sanskrit: vyasanāni ca sarvāṇi tyajethā bhūridakṣiṇa na caiva na prayuñjīta saṅgaṃ tu parivarjayet
english: And forsake all vices, O giver of bounteous gifts; not that he should wholly abstain from pleasures, but he should shun attachment to them.

sanskrit: nityaṃ hi vyasanī loke paribhūto bhavaty uta udvejayati lokaṃ cāpy atidveṣī mahīpatiḥ
english: For a man given to vice is ever despised in the world; and a ruler too full of hatred fills the world with dread.

sanskrit: bhavitavyaṃ sadā rājñā garbhiṇīsahadharmiṇā kāraṇaṃ ca mahārāja śṛṇu yenedam iṣyate
english: A king must always conduct himself after the manner of a pregnant woman, O great king; and hear the reason why this is enjoined.

sanskrit: yathā hi garbhiṇī hitvā svaṃ priyaṃ manaso 'nugam garbhasya hitam ādhatte tathā rājñāpy asaṃśayam
english: For just as a pregnant woman forsakes what her own heart finds pleasant and seeks instead the good of the child within her, so too must a king act, beyond all doubt.

sanskrit: vartitavyaṃ kuruśreṣṭha nityaṃ dharmānuvartinā svaṃ priyaṃ samabhityajya yad yal lokahitaṃ bhavet
english: A king who follows dharma, O best of the Kurus, must ever conduct himself thus, surrendering his own pleasure for whatever serves the good of the world.

sanskrit: na saṃtyājyaṃ ca te dhairyaṃ kadā cid api pāṇḍava dhīrasya spaṣṭadaṇḍasya na hy ājñā pratihanyate
english: And your firmness you must never abandon at any time, O Pāṇḍava; for the command of one who is resolute and unwavering in justice is never thwarted.

sanskrit: parihāsaś ca bhṛtyais te na nityaṃ vadatāṃ vara kartavyo rājaśārdūla doṣam atra hi me śṛṇu
english: And jesting with your servants must not be constant, O best of speakers; do not indulge in it, O tiger among kings—hear from me the fault therein.

sanskrit: avamanyanti bhartāraṃ saṃharṣād upajīvinaḥ sve sthāne na ca tiṣṭhanti laṅghayanti hi tad vacaḥ
english: Dependents grown over-familiar come to despise their master; they keep not to their proper place and transgress his word.

sanskrit: preṣyamāṇā vikalpante guhyaṃ cāpy anuyuñjate ayācyaṃ caiva yācante 'bhojyāny āhārayanti ca
english: When sent on errands they make objection; they pry into secrets, beg for what should not be begged, and have served to them food that ought not to be eaten.

sanskrit: krudhyanti paridīpyanti bhūmim adhyāsate 'sya ca utkocair vañcanābhiś ca kāryāṇy anuvihanti ca
english: They grow angry and blaze forth, they usurp his land, and by bribery and deceit they thwart the conduct of affairs.

sanskrit: jarjaraṃ cāsya viṣayaṃ kurvanti pratirūpakaiḥ strīr akṣibhiś ca sajjante tulyaveṣā bhavanti ca
english: They wear down his realm with counterfeits, they cling to women with wanton eyes, and they array themselves in dress equal to his own.

sanskrit: vātaṃ ca ṣṭhīvanaṃ caiva kurvate cāsya saṃnidhau nirlajjā naraśārdūla vyāharanti ca tadvacaḥ
english: Shameless, they break wind and spit in his very presence, O tiger among men, and openly mock his words.

sanskrit: hayaṃ vā dantinaṃ vāpi rathaṃ nṛpatisaṃmatam adhirohanty anādṛtya harṣule pārthive mṛdau
english: They mount, without leave, the horse, the elephant, or the chariot reserved for the king's own use, when the ruler is given to mirth and is soft of temper.

sanskrit: idaṃ te duṣkaraṃ rājann idaṃ te durviceṣṭitam ity evaṃ suhṛdo nāma bruvanti pariṣadgatāḥ
english: "This deed of yours, O king, was ill-done; this conduct of yours was unseemly"—thus, in the assembly, do men who pass for friends speak.

sanskrit: kruddhe cāsmin hasanty eva na ca hṛṣyanti pūjitāḥ saṃgharṣaśīlāś ca sadā bhavanty anyonyakāraṇāt
english: When he is angered they but laugh; honored, they take no pleasure; and they are ever quarrelsome, contending against one another for cause.

sanskrit: visraṃsayanti mantraṃ ca vivṛṇvanti ca duṣkṛtam līlayā caiva kurvanti sāvajñās tasya śāsanam alaṃkaraṇabhojyaṃ ca tathā snānānulepanam
english: They let his counsel leak away and lay bare his misdeeds; scornfully and in mere sport they carry out his command—even as to his ornaments and his food, his bath and his anointing.

sanskrit: helamānā naravyāghra svasthās tasyopaśṛṇvate nindanti svān adhīkārān saṃtyajanti ca bhārata
english: Heedless and at their ease, O tiger among men, they listen to him with contempt; they decry their own offices and forsake them, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: na vṛttyā parituṣyanti rājadeyaṃ haranti ca krīḍituṃ tena cecchanti sasūtreṇeva pakṣiṇā asmatpraṇeyo rājeti loke caiva vadanty uta
english: They are not content with their wages and seize what is the king's due; they wish to toy with him as with a bird held on a string, and they say abroad in the world, "This king is led by us."

sanskrit: ete caivāpare caiva doṣāḥ prādurbhavanty uta nṛpatau mārdavopete harṣule ca yudhiṣṭhira
english: These faults and many others besides arise, O Yudhiṣṭhira, when a king is given over to softness and to merriment.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca nityodyuktena vai rājñā bhavitavyaṃ yudhiṣṭhira praśāmyate ca rājā hi nārīvodyamavarjitaḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: A king must be ever exerting himself, O Yudhiṣṭhira; for a king bereft of effort fades away, like a woman left without a husband's care.

sanskrit: bhagavān uśanā cāha ślokam atra viśāṃ pate tam ihaikamanā rājan gadatas tvaṃ nibodha me
english: The blessed Uśanas spoke a verse upon this matter, O lord of peoples; with single mind, O king, mark it as I recite it to you here.

sanskrit: dvāv etau grasate bhūmiḥ sarpo bilaśayān iva rājānaṃ cāviroddhāraṃ brāhmaṇaṃ cāpravāsinam
english: These two the earth devours, as a serpent swallows the creatures that lodge in its holes: a king who offers no resistance, and a brāhmaṇa who never goes abroad.

sanskrit: tad etan naraśārdūla hṛdi tvaṃ kartum arhasi saṃdheyān api saṃdhatsva virodhyāṃś ca virodhaya
english: This, O tiger among men, you ought to lay to heart: make peace with those fit for peace, and set yourself against those to be opposed.

sanskrit: saptāṅge yaś ca te rājye vaiparītyaṃ samācaret gurur vā yadi vā mitraṃ pratihantavya eva saḥ
english: Whoever within your kingdom of seven limbs should act perversely against it—be he your teacher or your friend—he is to be struck down all the same.

sanskrit: maruttena hi rājñāyaṃ gītaḥ ślokaḥ purātanaḥ rājyādhikāre rājendra bṛhaspatimataḥ purā
english: For this ancient verse was sung by King Marutta of old, upon the governance of a kingdom, O king of kings, after the teaching of Bṛhaspati.

sanskrit: guror apy avaliptasya kāryākāryam ajānataḥ utpathapratipannasya parityāgo vidhīyate
english: Even a teacher, if he is arrogant and knows not what should and should not be done, who has strayed onto the wrong path—the forsaking of him is ordained.

sanskrit: bāhoḥ putreṇa rājñā ca sagareṇeha dhīmatā asamañjāḥ suto jyeṣṭhas tyaktaḥ paurahitaiṣiṇā
english: By the wise King Sagara, son of Bāhu, his eldest son Asamañja was cast off, for the sake of the welfare of the citizens.

sanskrit: asamañjāḥ sarayvāṃ prāk paurāṇāṃ bālakān nṛpa nyamajjayad ataḥ pitrā nirbhartsya sa vivāsitaḥ
english: Asamañja, of old, used to drown the children of the citizens in the Sarayū, O king; therefore his father rebuked him and sent him into exile.

sanskrit: ṛṣiṇoddālakenāpi śvetaketur mahātapāḥ mithyā viprān upacaran saṃtyakto dayitaḥ sutaḥ
english: By the seer Uddālaka too was Śvetaketu, of great austerity, his beloved son, cast off, for he had dealt falsely with the brāhmaṇas.

sanskrit: lokarañjanam evātra rājñāṃ dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ satyasya rakṣaṇaṃ caiva vyavahārasya cārjavam
english: Herein the eternal dharma of kings is just this: to give joy to the people, to safeguard truth, and to deal uprightly in all affairs.

sanskrit: na hiṃsyāt paravittāni deyaṃ kāle ca dāpayet vikrāntaḥ satyavāk kṣānto nṛpo na calate pathaḥ
english: He should not lay hands on others' wealth, and should cause what is due to be given in its season; valiant, truthful, and forbearing, such a king does not swerve from his path.

sanskrit: guptamantro jitakrodho śāstrārthagataniścayaḥ dharme cārthe ca kāme ca mokṣe ca satataṃ rataḥ
english: Keeping his counsel secret, having conquered wrath, settled in his grasp of the meaning of the treatises, ever devoted to dharma, artha, kāma, and mokṣa alike.

sanskrit: trayyā saṃvṛtarandhraś ca rājā bhavitum arhati vṛjinasya narendrāṇāṃ nānyat saṃvaraṇāt param
english: A king ought to have his weak points covered over by the three Vedas; for kings there is no better defense against wrongdoing than this concealment.

sanskrit: cāturvarṇyasya dharmāś ca rakṣitavyā mahīkṣitā dharmasaṃkararakṣā hi rājñāṃ dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ
english: The duties of the four orders must be guarded by the ruler of the earth; for to prevent the confusion of dharma is the eternal dharma of kings.

sanskrit: na viśvasec ca nṛpatir na cātyarthaṃ na viśvaset ṣāḍguṇyaguṇadoṣāṃś ca nityaṃ buddhyāvalokayet
english: A king should neither be over-trusting nor wholly without trust, and should ever weigh in his mind the merits and faults of the sixfold policy.

sanskrit: dviṭchidradarśī nṛpatir nityam eva praśasyate trivargaviditārthaś ca yuktacāropadhiś ca yaḥ
english: A king who marks the weak points of his foes is ever praised, who knows the import of the three aims and rightly employs spies and secret agents.

sanskrit: kośasyopārjanaratir yamavaiśravaṇopamaḥ vettā ca daśavargasya sthānavṛddhikṣayātmanaḥ
english: Devoted to the gathering of his treasury, the equal of Yama and Vaiśravaṇa, and a knower of the tenfold group concerning stability, growth, and decline.

sanskrit: abhṛtānāṃ bhaved bhartā bhṛtānāṃ cānvavekṣakaḥ nṛpatiḥ sumukhaś ca syāt smitapūrvābhibhāṣitā
english: He should be a supporter of the unprovided and a watchful guardian of those already in his service; and a king should be of pleasant countenance, addressing men with a smile.

sanskrit: upāsitā ca vṛddhānāṃ jitatandrīr alolupaḥ satāṃ vṛtte sthitamatiḥ santo hy ācāradarśinaḥ
english: A waiter upon the aged, one who has conquered sloth and is free of greed, his mind fixed in the conduct of the good; for the good are the very mirror of right conduct.

sanskrit: na cādadīta vittāni satāṃ hastāt kadā cana asadbhyas tu samādadyāt sadbhyaḥ saṃpratipādayet
english: And he should never at any time take wealth from the hands of the good; but from the wicked he may take it, and to the good he should bestow it.
